chunks: He said: Abu Bakr Muhammad ibn Umar al-Ji'abi reported to us, he said: Muhammad ibn Yahya ibn Sulaiman al-Marwazi reported to us, he said: Abdullah ibn Muhammad al-Ayshi reported to us, he said: Hammad ibn Salemah reported to us, from Ayyub, from Abu Qilabah, from Abu Hurairah, who said: The Messenger of God, peace be upon him and his family, said:

"This is the month of Ramadan, a blessed month whose fasts God has made obligatory. The gates of Paradise are opened in it and the devils are shackled in it. In it there is a night better than a thousand months. Whoever is deprived of it is indeed deprived."
He, peace be upon him and his family, repeated that three times.

key_terms.الجنان: Paradise (al-Jinan), the heavenly gardens promised to the righteous
key_terms.الشياطين: The devils (al-Shayatin), evil jinn who tempt humanity
key_terms.رمضان: Ramadan, the ninth month of the Islamic lunar calendar during which Muslims fast
key_terms.صيام: Fasting (sawm), abstaining from food, drink, and other specified acts from dawn to sunset
key_terms.ليلة: Night, referring here to Laylat al-Qadr (the Night of Decree)

ai.seo_question: What did the Prophet Muhammad say about the virtues of Ramadan?
ai.summary: The Prophet Muhammad (SAWW) extolled the virtues of the month of Ramadan, describing it as blessed with obligatory fasting, open gates of Paradise, restrained devils, and containing the Night of Qadr (Laylat al-Qadr), which is better than a thousand months. This hadith was narrated through Abu Hurairah and was so important that the Prophet repeated it three times to emphasize its significance to his companions.
